          # lib/libdartaotfah.so); the published v1.0.709 bundle broke every
          # machine-loop fa launch (dartaotruntime: "not an AOT snapshot",

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            runner: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-m5
            runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: '& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Fa\bin\fa.exe" --version'

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Unix)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_fa_clip.sh — compile the native `fa-clip` pasteboard helper (gh-2040).
#
# Usage: build_fa_clip.sh [<output-path>]
#
# The helper rides the macOS CLI bundles (bundle/bin/fa-clip, per-arch —
# the release matrix builds each arch on a native runner, gh-2040 AC8) and
# installs beside the `fa` binary, which resolves it relative to its own
# executable path. Exit 0 = binary written; exit 1 = no toolchain (callers
# treat a missing helper as the named pasteboard-unavailable path, AC5).

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$REPO_ROOT/tool/fa-clip/fa-clip.swift"
OUT="${1:-$REPO_ROOT/tool/fa-clip/fa-clip}"

if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
  echo "fa-clip is macOS-only — not building on $(uname -s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "swiftc not found — fa-clip not built (paste degrades to the named unavailable path, gh-2040 AC5)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "$(uname -m)" in
  arm64) target="arm64-apple-macos10.13" ;;
  x86_64) target="x86_64-apple-macos10.13" ;;
  *) echo "unsupported arch for fa-clip: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
swiftc -O -target "$target" -o "$OUT" "$SRC"
chmod +x "$OUT"
echo "built $OUT ($target)"

      - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (gh-2075, composite contract)
        uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.arch }}-macos
          package-roots: .

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        run: |
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # gh-2120 follow-up: the entry is BUILT as `fa` (bin/fa.dart), not
          # renamed — on Dart >=3.14 (native linux) the bundle is split
          # (thin launcher + libdartaot<exe>.so) and a post-build mv
          # desyncs the pair (`dartaotruntime: not an AOT snapshot`).
          if [ "${{ matrix.arch }}" = "x64" ]; then
            arch -x86_64 dart build cli --target=bin/fa.dart --output=build/out
          else
            dart build cli --target=bin/fa.dart --output=build/out
          fi
          chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary
        run: |
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-2040: the native fa-clip pasteboard helper rides the macOS CLI
      # bundle (bundle/bin/fa-clip, per-arch — this matrix builds each arch
      # on a native runner, AC8) so install.sh / fa update ship it beside
      # the binary and image paste never rides Apple Events.
      - name: Build fa-clip pasteboard helper (gh-2040)
        run: |
          if [ "${{ matrix.arch }}" = "x64" ]; then
            arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          else
            bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          fi
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          test -x build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip

      - name: Archive and upload CLI bundle
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=build-macos-cli — the leg-suffixed
          # draft owner identity keeps the guard below scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never the sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2408 `[ci-red] v1.0.775 failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.775 tag run (https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/45524011164) went red on `Build native binaries (self-hosted, macos-m5, macos, x64, tar)` and `Advance vpinned marker`.

**Root cause**: commit ea42d8f (#2405, the macOS-runner migration) routes the x64 macOS CLI leg to the self-hosted `macos-m5` pool, where PATH prefers Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/bin` — which contains an **ARM64-only** `bash` (`shell: /opt/homebrew/bin/bash` in the run log). The fa-clip step invokes `arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...`; `arch` resolves `bash` via PATH and `posix_spawnp` refuses to run the arm64-only binary as x86_64: `arch: posix_spawnp: bash: Bad CPU type in executable` (job 138910839290, step "Build fa-clip pasteboard helper (macOS, gh-2040)"). On the GitHub-hosted `macos-15-intel` runners this pattern used to work because PATH resolved to the universal `/bin/bash`.

**Why the sibling legs are fine**: `arch -x86_64 dart build cli ...` works because `dart-lang/setup-dart` installs the **x64** SDK (`architecture: ${{ matrix.arch }}`), so `dart` is a real x86_64 binary; the "Build CLI bundle" step was green in the failed run, proving Rosetta execution itself works on macos-m5. The arm64 fa-clip leg (same pool, native swiftc) was green, proving swiftc exists on the pool.

**Impact**: the x64 macOS CLI tarball (`fa-macos-x64.tar.gz`) never builds or uploads; the release matrix stays red; `release-provenance` cannot publish the signed SHA256SUMS (it needs the full matrix); and `Advance vpinned marker` (`install-pin-bump`, runs with `always()`) then fails its own fail-closed pre-move provenance gate: `E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release v1.0.775 publishes no SHA256SUMS ... marker NOT moved`. That second failure is **by design** (ci.yml comment: pin_release.sh "fails the job loudly instead of moving the marker") — the marker correctly stayed at v1.0.774; it is not an independent bug. Same latent break exists in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (`build-macos-cli` x64 leg) and would red the next macOS release build the same way.

**Fix approach**: pin the Rosetta interpreter to macOS's **universal** `/bin/bash` — `arch -x86_64 /bin/bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...` — in `ci.yml` (release `binaries` job) and `build-macos.yml` (`build-macos-cli`). `/bin/bash` ships universal (x86_64+arm64) on every supported macOS, so `arch -x86_64` can never again resolve an ARM-only interpreter from PATH. Under Rosetta, `uname -m` in `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` reports `x86_64`, so it still emits the `x86_64-apple-macos10.13` target as intended; `swiftc` (universal, Xcode CLT) runs under Rosetta exactly like the already-green x64 dart build. No product code changes; no change to `pin_release.sh` (it behaved exactly as designed).

**Recovery**: after this fix merges to main, the 2h coalesce tick cuts the next annotated tag (v1.0.776) from main and the full release run executes with the fixed workflow — binaries green → provenance publishes signed SHA256SUMS → `install-pin-bump` advances the marker. Re-running the stale v1.0.775 run would not help (a rerun uses the tag's original workflow file).

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for this ticket.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

./outputs/rca.md:7:**Root cause**: commit ea42d8f (#2405, the macOS-runner migration) routes the x64 macOS CLI leg to the self-hosted `macos-m5` pool, where PATH prefers Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/bin` — which contains an **ARM64-only** `bash` (`shell: /opt/homebrew/bin/bash` in the run log). The fa-clip step invokes `arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...`; `arch` resolves `bash` via PATH and `posix_spawnp` refuses to run the arm64-only binary as x86_64: `arch: posix_spawnp: bash: Bad CPU type in executable` (job 138910839290, step "Build fa-clip pasteboard helper (macOS, gh-2040)"). On the GitHub-hosted `macos-15-intel` runners this pattern used to work because PATH resolved to the universal `/bin/bash`.

The arm64 fa-clip leg (same pool, native swiftc) was green, proving swiftc exists on the pool.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The v1.0.775 `binaries` macos-x64 leg (PR #2405's move to the self-hosted macos-m5 pool) runs the fa-clip step as `arch -x86_64 bash ...`. On macos-m5, PATH resolves `bash` to the **ARM64-only** Homebrew build (`/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`), so `arch` died with `posix_spawnp: bash: Bad CPU type in executable` (job 138910839290) — on the old hosted `macos-15-intel` runners PATH resolved to the universal `/bin/bash`, so the pattern used to pass. The `Advance vpinned marker` failure is the by-design knock-on: with the matrix red, `release-provenance` never published signed SHA256SUMS and `pin_release.sh` correctly refused to move the marker (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`) — the marker stayed at v1.0.774, as designed.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (release `binaries` job) and `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (`build-macos-cli`): `arch -x86_64 /bin/bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...` — pin the Rosetta interpreter to macOS's universal `/bin/bash` so PATH can never resolve an ARM-only one again. No product code, no change to `pin_release.sh`.
- Under Rosetta, `uname -m` still reports `x86_64`, so `build_fa_clip.sh` keeps emitting the `x86_64-apple-macos10.13` helper; the already-green x64 `dart build cli` proves Rosetta execution works on this pool.

### Test Coverage

- `test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart` (new, static workflow-shape guard): every `arch -x86_64 <cmd>` in every workflow must be an absolute path or bare `dart` (the setup-dart exact-arch-SDK exemption, itself pinned per-job) — RED before the fix (3 failures on the exact broken sites), GREEN after; 4/4 pass.
- Workflow-shape family: `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test`, `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test`, `ci_1596`, `fetch_shape_guard` — 69 passed. Full suite: green (see CI).

### Notes

- No `Fixes/Closes` keywords per repo policy; the ci-red issue closes when the ref goes green. Rerunning the stale v1.0.775 run won't help (a rerun uses the tag's original workflow) — the next coalesce tick cuts v1.0.776 from main after merge, and the full release chain (binaries → provenance SHA256SUMS → marker advance) executes green.
- Residual assumption: `swiftc` (universal in Xcode CLT) runs under Rosetta exactly like the x64 dart build already does on macos-m5; the arm64 fa-clip leg (native swiftc) was green in the same run.

fix(ci): gh-2408 — pin the Rosetta fa-clip interpreter to universal /bin/bash

v1.0.775's binaries macos-x64 leg (PR #2405's self-hosted macos-m5
migration) ran `arch -x86_64 bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh ...`; PATH on
the macos-m5 pool resolves `bash` to the ARM-only Homebrew build, so arch
died with `posix_spawnp: bash: Bad CPU type in executable`
(run 45524011164, job 138910839290). The release chain red'd from there:
no fa-macos-x64 tarball -> no signed SHA256SUMS (release-provenance needs
the full matrix) -> the vpinned marker advance fail-closed
(E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING; the marker stayed at v1.0.774 BY DESIGN).

- ci.yml (release binaries) + build-macos.yml (build-macos-cli): invoke
  the fa-clip build with the universal /bin/bash under Rosetta - PATH can
  never resolve an ARM-only interpreter again. Under Rosetta `uname -m`
  still reports x86_64, so build_fa_clip.sh keeps emitting the
  x86_64-apple-macos10.13 target; the already-green x64 `dart build cli`
  proves Rosetta execution works on the pool.
- test/ci_2408_rosetta_interpreter_guard_test.dart: repo-wide
  workflow-shape guard - every `arch -x86_64 <cmd>` in every workflow
  must be an absolute path or bare `dart` (the setup-dart exact-arch SDK
  exemption, itself pinned per-job).
- CHANGELOG.md: curated Unreleased entry.
